name: Apple II Plus
credits: Layout after the Apple II Plus (1979) keyboard; colours after its beige case and dark brown and black caps.
notes: Faithful: the II Plus's 52 keys in their rows and order (ESC beside Q and CTRL beside A, as on the machine), the shifted legends printed above the characters, BELL on G, upper-case legends on dark brown letter keys and near-black function keys, and a blank space bar. The II Plus has no lower case; here a letter types lower case, SHIFT types upper case (except P, N and M, which type @, ^ and ] as on the machine), and a double tap on SHIFT locks it, a caps lock the machine never had. ← erases the last character, which is what it did while you typed a line; → moves the caret right. There is no left arrow, as on the machine (← is the erase key in both layers), so a single-key game that wants one needs another skin. Approximated: widths are compressed to fit a phone and the keys are drawn rather than photographed. Mapped to none: RESET (it rebooted the machine), REPT (decorative: letters do not repeat when held here, only ← and → do, and REPT does not make them; its cap has no second legend, so none is drawn) and CTRL (there is no control-key layer). The POWER lamp is not drawn, since a skin has no decorative elements.
